'''Geerat J. Vermeij''' (born September 28, 1946) is a [[Netherlands|Dutch]]-born [[Paleoecology|paleoecologist]] and [[Evolutionary biology|evolutionary biologist]] in the Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences at the [[University of California at Davis|University of California, Davis]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Fong |first=Janice |date=2018-05-01 |title=Geerat J. Vermeij |url=https://eps.ucdavis.edu/people/faculty/vermeij |access-date=2022-10-24 |website=UC Davis Earth and Planetary Sciences |language=en}}</ref> He studies marine [[molluscs]], both as fossils and as living creatures, as well as influence creatures have on each other's evolutionary fates, alongside having worked on plants, crabs, extinction, biological invasions, and biogeography.<ref name="shapeoflife.org">{{Cite web |title=Geerat Vermeij, Evolutionary Biologist {{!}} Shape of Life |url=https://www.shapeoflife.org/scientist/geerat-vermeij-evolutionary-biologist |access-date=2023-05-24 |website=www.shapeoflife.org}}</ref> He received a [[MacArthur Fellowship]] in 1992,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.blind.net/g5000005.htm |title=Blind Professor Receives Macarthur Award |access-date=2009-09-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090530170828/http://www.blind.net/g5000005.htm |archive-date=2009-05-30 }}</ref> and in 2000, was awarded the [[Daniel Giraud Elliot Medal]] from the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="Elliot">{{cite web|title=Daniel Giraud Elliot Medal |url=http://www.nasonline.org/site/PageServer?pagename=AWARDS_elliot |publisher=National Academy of Sciences |access-date=15 February 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120801121352/http://nas.nasonline.org/site/PageServer?pagename=AWARDS_elliot |archive-date=August 1, 2012 }}</ref> He was also a fellow of the [[California Academy of Sciences]] in 1992 and was awarded the Fellows Medal from the [[California Academy of Sciences]] in 2017.<ref name=":4" />

==Early life and education==
Vermeij was born  in [[Sappemeer]], [[Netherlands]]. Blind from the age of three, he studied [[Braille]] at the Prins Alexander Stichting Boarding School in [[Huis ter Heide, Utrecht|Huis Ter Heide]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Vermeij {{!}} NCBYS |url=https://blindscience.org/vermeij |access-date=2022-10-24 |website=blindscience.org |archive-date=2024-05-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240521064505/https://blindscience.org/vermeij }}</ref> He moved from the Netherlands to [[Nutley, New Jersey]] at age 10, and graduated from [[Nutley High School]] in 1965.<ref>[http://nutleyhalloffame.nutleypubliclibrary.org/2003-vermeij/ 2003 Hall of Fame Inductee, Geerat J. Vermeij], Nutley Hall of Fame. Accessed November 9, 2019. "Geerat J. Vermeij is one of the world's preeminent scientists in ecology, malacology and biology. Born in Holland, he came to America, lived in Nutley and graduated from Nutley High School in the Class of 1965."</ref><ref name=":1" /> Since the age of 10, Vermeij wanted to be a [[Conchology|conchologist]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=2014-01-22 |title=Geerat Vermeij, Evolutionary Biologist |url=https://www.shapeoflife.org/scientist/geerat-vermeij-evolutionary-biologist |access-date=2022-10-24 |website=www.shapeoflife.org |language=en}}</ref> Vermeij had a school teacher who once brought shells from Florida. There were great differences in the characteristics of those shells and the ones he experienced in the [[Netherlands]], which sparked his interest.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-01-03 |title=A feeling for the fossil record: an interview with Geerat Vermeij - Understanding Evolution |url=https://evolution.berkeley.edu/a-feeling-for-the-fossil-record-an-interview-with-geerat-vermeij/ |access-date=2023-05-24 |language=en-US}}</ref>

He has a wife, Edith Zipser, and a daughter, Hermine.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Vermeij {{!}} NCBYS |url=https://blindscience.org/vermeij |access-date=2023-05-24 |website=blindscience.org |archive-date=2024-05-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240521064505/https://blindscience.org/vermeij }}</ref> His vision loss did not slow him down. He travelled the world with research assistants to retrieve shells. His interests in comparing shell traits came his senior year at Princeton University when he took a trip to both [[Costa Rica]] and [[Hawaii]]. There was a sharp contrast in the molluscs and it intrigued him.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ravindran |first=Sandeep |date=2023-01-31 |title=QnAs with Geerat J. Vermeij |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |language=en |volume=120 |issue=5 |article-number=e2220273120 |doi=10.1073/pnas.2220273120 |issn=0027-8424 |pmc=9945939 |pmid=36693096 |bibcode=2023PNAS..12020273R }}</ref> Vermeij proceeded to graduate from [[Princeton University]] in 1968 and received his Ph.D. in [[biology]] and [[geology]] from [[Yale University]] in 1971.

==Career==
Vermeij studies [[Evolutionary arms race|coevolutionary]] relationships between predator and prey organisms, with a focus on marine [[Mollusca|mollusks]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /> His research argues that an important evolutionary mechanism is the process of escalation, which occurs when species adapt to, or are limited by their competitors, [[Predation|predators]], and [[Parasitism|parasites]].<ref name="J. 1987">{{Cite book |first=Geerat J. |last=Vermeij  |title=Evolution and escalation: an ecological history of life |date=1987 |publisher=Princeton Univ. Press |isbn=0-691-08446-7 |oclc=230867068}}</ref>

In lieu of sight, Vermeij uses his sense of touch to better understand mollusk morphology.<ref name=":1" /> Throughout his career, he has challenged the assumption that people with disabilities like blindness cannot conduct scientific research.

As part of his professional career, he has been a part of multiple professional societies including the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], the [[Society for the Study of Evolution]], [[Paleontological Society]], [[American Society of Naturalists]], the Institute of Malacology, [[Nederlandse Malacologische Vereniging]], and [[:nl:Werkgroep voor Tertiaire en Kwartaire Geologie|Werkgroep voor Tertiaire en Kwartiaire Geologie]]. He was a member of the board of trustees at the [[California Academy of Sciences]] from 2006 to 2015.

Vermeij has over 300 publications and 5 published books including his first book, ''Biogeography and Adaptation'' published in 1978.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Vermeij |first=Geerat J. |url=https://www.hup.harvard.edu/catalog.php?isbn=9780674073760 |title=Biogeography and Adaptation: Patterns of Marine Life |date=1978-01-01 |publisher=Harvard University Press |isbn=978-0-674-07376-0 |location=Cambridge, MA}}</ref> He has also published ''Evolution and Escalation: An Ecological History of Life, A Natural History of Shells'', ''Privileged Hands: A Scientific Life,''<ref name="shapeoflife.org"/> and ''Nature: An Economic History'', which evaluates economics and evolution.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |date=2018-05-01 |title=Geerat J. Vermeij |url=https://eps.ucdavis.edu/people/faculty/vermeij |access-date=2023-05-24 |website=UC Davis Earth and Planetary Sciences |language=en}}</ref> His forthcoming book is titled ''The Evolution of Power.''<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://press.princeton.edu/books/hardcover/9780691250410/the-evolution-of-power |title=The Evolution of Power |date=2023-11-14 |isbn=978-0-691-25041-0 |language=en |last1=Vermeij |first1=Geerat }}</ref>

In February 2023, Distinguished Professor Emeritus Geerat Vermeij in the Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences, UC Davis, delivered the New Emeriti Distinguished Lecture, focusing on ''The Evolution of Power''.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-01-23 |title=Geerat Vermeij to Give New Emeriti Distinguished Lecture on 'The Evolution of Power' |url=https://lettersandscience.ucdavis.edu/news/geerat-vermeij-give-new-emeriti-distinguished-lecture-evolution-power |access-date=2023-05-24 |website=UC Davis College of Letters and Science |language=en}}</ref>

=== Eponymy ===
The gastropod genus ''[[Vermeijius]]'' has been named in his honor.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kantor |first=Yuri I. |last2=Fedosov |first2=Alexander E. |last3=Snyder |first3=Martin Avery |last4=Bouchet |first4=Philippe |date=2018-05-07 |title=Pseudolatirus Bellardi, 1884 revisited, with the description of two new genera and five new species (Neogastropoda: Fasciolariidae) |url=https://europeanjournaloftaxonomy.eu/index.php/ejt/article/view/562 |journal=European Journal of Taxonomy |language=en |issue=433 |doi=10.5852/ejt.2018.433  |doi-access=free|issn=2118-9773}}</ref>
